_readme: Suggestions for how The Co.LLab™ can improve its IP and support the Omnidirectional Enterprise™ ecosystem. Each one stays 'new' in the owner's IP review page until the owner decides (considering, planned, done or declined, with a note), and a weekly email lists whatever is still undecided. Edit this file to add ideas; decisions are kept separately so they are never lost.

items.title: One Legacy Statement per member
items.why: Members finish several separate tools. One statement that joins their four-phase answers (mission, structure, practice, preservation) makes the legacy tangible and gives them one document to carry forward.
items.firstStep: Assemble it from the quest answers already saved in each member's portal.

items.title: Phase Readiness view in the portal
items.why: Each quest already produces a phase map. Combining them shows a member where their whole organization is strong or thin across The IV Phases™, not just one tool at a time.
items.firstStep: Add a portal panel that totals the phase maps from every completed quest.

items.title: 30, 90 and 365-day commitment check-ins
items.why: Every quest ends with a commitment. Emailing it back later and asking what happened keeps the practice alive and tells us which parts of the IP actually change behavior.
items.firstStep: Schedule a check-in email from each completed quest and record the reply.

items.title: Team mode: several leaders, one quest
items.why: Alignment gaps show up when leaders answer separately and then compare. Organizations buy the IP for the whole team, not one person.
items.firstStep: Let a member invite colleagues to the same quest and show where answers differ.

items.title: Industry editions of the Diagnostic
items.why: Nonprofits, creators and small businesses use different words for the same infrastructure. Editions would keep the model and change the language, and show which Omnidirectional Enterprise™ direction each serves.
items.firstStep: Start with a Nonprofit edition and a Small Business edition of the Diagnostic.

items.title: Facilitator guide for running a quest with a team
items.why: Many leaders will want to run a quest in a meeting. A short guide keeps the structure and the language consistent.
items.firstStep: Write a one-page facilitator guide for the Foundation Strength Snapshot™.

items.title: Public changelog: what changed because of member feedback
items.why: Transparency builds trust and shows members their feedback is considered. It also gives the IP a visible history.
items.firstStep: Publish an entry whenever a feedback item is marked done.

items.title: A free Succession quest
items.why: Preservation is the phase members most often leave thin across most organizations. A free starting point would bring more leaders into it.
items.firstStep: Draft it from the Knowledge Transfer Checklist™ and the Continuity Quick Check™; confirm against real quest data first.

items.title: Introductions between collaborating companies
items.why: Collaborating Companies shows who is here. Introductions let one member ask to work with another, which is how value starts to move in every direction.
items.firstStep: Add a Request an intro button to each company page that emails the listed contact.

items.title: Collaborating Companies filters by Omnidirectional Enterprise™ direction
items.why: Members should be able to find who can carry, fund, teach or buy from them: Businesses, Nonprofits, Communities, People, Technology, Capital, Knowledge + IP and Creators.
items.firstStep: Tag each listing with its directions and add filters.

items.title: Member-to-member offers
items.why: Opt-in offers between members (clearly labeled, set by the member) turn Collaborating Companies into real commerce, and make the value of a license and Membership visible.
items.firstStep: Let a listing carry an optional member offer with terms the member writes.

items.title: Connect Collaborating Companies to Impact and community partners
items.why: Nonprofits and communities are two of the eight directions. Listing partners and skills requests would keep that direction active, not just named.
items.firstStep: Add a Nonprofit and Community category with skill or volunteer requests.

items.title: Successor and apprentice matching
items.why: Leaders who are preparing to hand on their work could meet members who want to carry it forward.
items.firstStep: Add an optional Seeking a successor or Seeking an apprenticeship flag on listings.

items.title: An annual Omnidirectional Enterprise™ report
items.why: A yearly, anonymous summary of how value moved between members (introductions made, offers used, counts only) would show the ecosystem working. Only real numbers, never estimates.
items.firstStep: Start counting introductions and offers now so the data exists.
